paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
caption: Proportion of SDPA output values below threshold after gating (Left: 1e-2, Right: 1e-3). We also include sparsity measurements obtained by multiplying the average gating score with pre-gating hidden states.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: Тази линейна диаграма илюстрира промяната в спарситета на изхода на SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) по слоеве при праг 1e-3, като сравнява три различни сценария: спарситета преди прилагане на гейтинга, след прилагане на гейтинга и след умножаване на средния гейтинг скър с предварителните скрити състояния. Оста X, означена като „Layer“, представлява номера на слоя и е линейна, с диапазон от 0 до около 23, с етикети през интервали от 5. Оста Y, означена като „Sparsity Ratio“, е с линейна скала и диапазон от 0.0 до 0.8, с етикети през 0.2. Първата линия — синя пунктирана — представлява „sparsity ratio before gate“ и започва при около 0.03 при слой 0, след което спада леко и остава почти постоянна около 0.01 до края на диаграмата. Втората линия — оранжева точкована — „sparsity ratio after gate“ започва при около 0.8 при слой 0, спада бързо до около 0.1 при слой 5, след това по-бавно до около 0.03 при слой 10 и остава на ниско ниво с леки колебания до края. Третата линия — зелена пунктирана — „sparsity ratio after average gate“ започва при около 0.7 при слой 0, спада до около 0.1 при слой 5, след това до около 0.02 при слой 10 и остава на ниско ниво с леки колебания до края. Всички три линии имат посочени средни стойности в легендата: 0.003, 0.126 и 0.080 съответно.
model_annotations.Chinese: This line chart illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA output across model layers under a threshold of 1e-3, comparing three conditions: sparsity before gating, sparsity after gating, and sparsity after applying an average gate. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to approximately 22 with linear spacing and integer tick marks at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.8 with linear scaling and tick marks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. The blue dashed line representing “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.003” remains near zero across all layers, starting at approximately 0.02 at layer 0 and gradually declining to near 0.0 by layer 22. The orange dotted line, “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126,” begins at approximately 0.83 at layer 0, drops sharply to 0.4 at layer 2, continues decreasing to 0.15 at layer 5, and stabilizes near 0.02–0.05 from layer 10 onward, with minor fluctuations including a small peak near 0.08 at layer 20. The green dash-dot line, “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.080,” starts at approximately 0.78 at layer 0, declines steeply to 0.2 at layer 2, reaches 0.1 at layer 4, and then gradually decreases to near 0.02 by layer 10, remaining low with slight oscillations through layer 22.
model_annotations.English: This line plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output across model layers, using a threshold of 1e-3. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to approximately 22 with linear spacing and integer tick labels. The y-axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.8 with linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Three distinct lines are plotted: a blue dashed line representing “sparsity ratio before gate,” which remains near zero across all layers (starting at ~0.02 and decreasing to ~0.005); an orange dotted line for “sparsity ratio after gate,” which begins at ~0.82 at layer 0, drops sharply to ~0.15 by layer 5, then gradually declines to ~0.02 by layer 22; and a green dash-dot line for “sparsity ratio after average gate,” which starts at ~0.78, falls steeply to ~0.10 by layer 5, and continues declining to ~0.01 by layer 22. The legend also reports average sparsity ratios over all layers: 0.003 for before gate, 0.126 for after gate, and 0.080 for after average gate.
model_annotations.German: The line chart illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output values below a threshold of 1e-3, plotted across model layers from 0 to approximately 22. The x-axis, labeled “Layer,” is linearly scaled with tick marks at intervals of 5, ranging from 0 to 22. The y-axis, labeled “Sparsity Ratio,” is linearly scaled from 0.0 to 0.8, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Three distinct lines are plotted: a blue dashed line representing the sparsity ratio before gating, which remains near zero across all layers (starting at approximately 0.02 and declining slightly to near 0.005); an orange dotted line representing the sparsity ratio after gating, which begins near 0.83 at layer 0, drops sharply to below 0.2 by layer 5, continues declining to near 0.03 by layer 10, and fluctuates slightly between 0.02 and 0.08 for layers 15 to 22; and a green dash-dot line representing the sparsity ratio after applying the average gate, which starts near 0.78 at layer 0, falls steeply to below 0.2 by layer 5, continues decreasing to approximately 0.02 by layer 10, and remains near 0.01–0.02 for layers 15 to 22, with minor fluctuations. The legend indicates average sparsity ratios across layers: 0.003 for before gating, 0.126 for after gating, and 0.080 for after average gating.
